catalyst_text: Reported negative topline Phase 3 results in TED
detailed_catalyst_text: Two Phase 3 studies in thyroid eye disease failed to meet the prespecified primary endpoint of proptosis responder rate at Week 24. Safety findings were consistent with prior experience and no new safety signals were identified.
catalyst_text_evidence: Immunovant's Phase 3 studies of batoclimab in thyroid eye disease (TED) each failed to meet their primary endpoint; safety results were consistent with previous findings. Based on the pre-specified statistical analysis plan, the studies failed to meet their primary endpoint of ≥2mm proptosis responder rate at Week 24, following 12 weeks of high-dose and 12 weeks of low-dose batoclimab treatment. Safety results were consistent with previous findings, and no new safety signals were identified.

catalyst_text: NDA accepted priority review PDUFA in Q3 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA for brepocitinib in dermatomyositis and granted Priority Review, assigning a PDUFA action date in the third quarter of 2026. This marks a key regulatory milestone supported by positive Phase 3 VALOR results in this serious autoimmune disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: Priovant Therapeutics today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted its New Drug Application (NDA) for brepocitinib for the treatment of dermatomyositis (DM) and has granted the application Priority Review. The FDA has assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date in the third quarter of calendar year 2026.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2 results in cutaneous sarcoidosis
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline data were reported from a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study in cutaneous sarcoidosis, showing significant improvements on CSAMI-A and IGA. The treatment was well tolerated with no serious adverse events. This represents a notable advancement in a disease with no approved therapies and historically limited clinical success.
catalyst_text_evidence: Priovant Therapeutics today announced positive results from the Phase 2 BEACON study evaluating brepocitinib in cutaneous sarcoidosis (CS). On the Cutaneous Sarcoidosis Activity and Morphology Instrument – Activity score (CSAMI-A), brepocitinib 45 mg achieved a 22.3-point mean improvement at Week 16 versus a 0.7-point improvement in placebo (Δ21.6 P<0.0001). On the Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA), 69% of brepocitinib 45 mg patients achieved the gold standard two-point improvement to Clear (0) / Almost Clear (1), compared to 0% of placebo patients (Δ 69% P=.0047). Brepocitinib was well tolerated during the study treatment period, with no Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) and all Adverse Events (AEs) graded mild or moderate in severity.
